changes.after: Build changed source code before running the updated program.

before: A compiler checks source code and translates it into a program the machine can run. A compilation error means no valid executable was produced from that attempt; it is different from a failure while a program runs.
#include <iostream> makes standard stream declarations available. std::cout is the output stream in the std namespace; :: selects a name from that namespace.
int main() is the entry function for this program. Its braces contain the instructions. Reaching the end of main returns a success status of zero.
The output below appears when the built executable runs, not merely when the source file is saved. A changed source file must be rebuilt before the executable reflects that edit.
Expected output or behavior: 3. Local compiler test evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Save a complete example as main.cpp in a new practice folder. With GCC already installed, compile g++ -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.cpp -o example, then run the produced executable. Change one value and compare running before versus after rebuilding. You may trace this without a compiler; finishing the reading is not proof of a local run.
after: Source code is the text you write. A compiler checks it and translates it into machine code. Building combines the needed pieces into an executable, a program file the computer can run.
#include <iostream> makes the standard stream declarations available. A declaration tells C++ about a name it can use. std::cout names the output stream in the std namespace.
Execution starts in main. Its braces contain the steps. In C++, reaching the end of main without a return statement gives a success status of zero.
Saving source text does not run the program. Output appears when the built executable runs.
The program prints 3 and starts a new line. There is no separate printed value for main's success status.
After changing the source, build it again before running. If compilation fails, that attempt produces no updated executable. An older executable may still exist and still show the old behavior.

before.question: You edit the output value but run the old executable without rebuilding. What should you expect?
choices: The executable automatically rereads the source text.
It can still show the old result because it contains the earlier compiled program.
before.explanation: Editing source and rebuilding an executable are separate actions.

after.question: You edit the output value but run the old executable without rebuilding. What can happen?
choices: It still shows the old result.
Saving the source already ran the new program.
after.explanation: The executable contains the earlier built code. Editing source does not update it automatically.

changes.before: C++ Core v1, standard C++23 features checked against the available GCC14.2 implementation. This app provides concept reading and an understanding check, not a C++ browser runner. Local example tests are separate evidence and do not certify learner mastery.
changes.after: The browser shows C++ code and checks your understanding; it does not run C++. Optional local examples use C++23.
